author: c2-sql-sme-critic (independent PostgreSQL SME critic subagent, fresh context, read-only; reviewed commit 8a7daa17)

findings.claim: Shared SQLCHK.explain, branch 'invalid input syntax for type': it always says 'a value does not fit its column. Text goes in single quotes; numbers and NULL do not.' On this page the likely trigger is a fallback of the wrong type, such as COALESCE(fee, 'Not priced') or CASE WHEN fee IS NULL THEN 'none' ELSE fee END. The simulator then shows ERROR: invalid input syntax for type numeric: "Not priced". No column is being stored, and the quotes are correct; the cause is that every COALESCE or CASE result must convert to one common type, here numeric. The plain-language advice sends the learner to the wrong fix.

evidence.section: PostgreSQL 19 (current): 10.5 UNION, CASE, and Related Constructs: "Convert all inputs to the final candidate type. Fail if there is not an implicit conversion from a given input type to the candidate type."
PostgreSQL 19 (current): 9.19.2 COALESCE: "The COALESCE function returns the first of its arguments that is not null."

findings.recommendation: Add a COALESCE/CASE-aware sentence to that branch, for example: 'If this comes from COALESCE or CASE, all its values must be the same kind: a numeric column needs a number fallback, and a text label needs a text column.' Or detect a coalesce or case in the failing statement and say that.
